label: Donor human milk
comment: Human milk, not cow's: only the pasteurising is the same idea.

about.text: Milk given by screened mothers to a milk bank, heated gently and handed out on prescription to babies, mostly premature ones, whose own mothers cannot supply enough. The first milk bank is credited to Vienna in 1909 and the first American one to the Boston Floating Hospital the year after.

sources.text: Human milk, given by mothers to milk banks: not part of the world’s farmed milk. My own rough estimate.

facts.v: Healthy, still lactating, tested negative for HIV, hepatitis and syphilis (VDRL), chest X-ray or tine test (Wikipedia, US-style; national rules differ)
Milk from several donors is pooled before it is pasteurised (a Canadian milk bank)
62.5 °C for 30 minutes, then cooled to 4 °C over 60 minutes (Milk Matters, Cape Town)
